content: Have you ever wondered why we feel so safe when it's raining heavily outside? Imagine a little boy named Chhotu who just came to Mumbai for the first time. He had nowhere to go, no roof over his head, and it started to rain. How did a simple cement pipe become his house?
What do you think is the difference between a 'house' and a 'home'? If you build walls with bricks, does it automatically become a home? Take a moment to guess!

content.title: Chhotu's Pipe House
content.description: Chhotu divided a large cement pipe into different parts: a place to sleep, a place to cook, and a place to dry clothes.

content: A 'House' (Makaan) is just a building made of bricks, cement, and wood. But a 'Home' (Ghar) is made of family, love, and care! Chhotu made a house out of a pipe, but it became a true home when he invited his friend Monu to live with him.

content.definition: A safe place that gives protection from bad weather or danger.

question: What is the main difference between a house and a home?
options: A house is bigger than a home
A home is made with family and love
They are exactly the same thing

content: Think about your own home. Explain in your own words to your parents: Which is your favorite part of your home and why? Have you noticed that some uninvited guests like ants, lizards, or spiders also live in your house?

content.mistake: Thinking that only humans build houses.
content.correction: Animals and insects also build homes to protect themselves! A bird's nest and a bee's hive are their homes.

content: Just like humans need a home for shelter from rain, sun, and cold, animals also need shelters. A house is divided into parts like the Kitchen (for cooking), Bedroom (for sleeping), and Bathroom (for washing). Our connections to these rooms make our daily lives run smoothly.

content.tip: Ask students to list out 3 uninvited animal guests in their home and discuss why we should keep our house clean to avoid pests.

content.description: Draw a picture of your house and decorate it just like we do during festivals (like Diwali or Eid). Label the different parts of your house like the kitchen, bedroom, and drawing room.
